content.text: {"grade":6,"complete":false,"main_gap":"The refinement lemma’s graph argument incorrectly infers global acyclicity from having fewer edges than vertices, though selecting a component with fewer edges than vertices repairs it.","errors":[{"description":"A multigraph with fewer edges than vertices can still contain a cycle or loop in one component while another component is a tree. Thus the component containing a_q need not be bipartite. Repair: since total edges are below total vertices, some component has e_C<v_C; connectedness then forces it to be a tree, and that component can be used.","quote":"Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on v vertices already uses at least v edges; hence every connected component C has e_C=v_C-1 and is a tree"}],"notes":"Apart from this local but essential error, the drafting lemma, refinement construction, subset-sum upper bound, and binary lower-bound construction form a coherent complete solution. The graph defect is straightforwardly repairable without changing the result."}
